authorization_instruction: continue from here to as far as you can. dont stop for reports. you know i trust in your recommendations. complete the bootstraps if possible. but if you absolutely require my input for something thats a design choice that hasnt been decided yet, then defer it and build around it - if possible.

authoring.title: The certified planner selects a constrained support-expanding catch target
authoring.claim: In the exact certified BR10.0 fixtures, the strict planner seals one immutable configuration, ranks a finite candidate set deterministically, retains a conservative actuator-limited contact clock, rejects collision and deadline failures specifically, returns an honest no-catch result when every candidate is infeasible, refuses configuration mutation and non-BRACE requests, and requests a genuinely new support contact without inventing contact, bearing, root rescue, foot pinning, pose teleport, or automatic guidance.
authoring.scope: Only the exact planner configuration, candidate fields, digests, reach-time calculation, collision witness, deadline reserve, support-improvement score, assistance exclusions, source, and BR10.0 program scope certified by br10_20260723T181129Z_980549f8.
authoring.mechanism: The planner filters each finite candidate through new-contact, collision, friction, torque, reach, deadline, clearance, distance, and support-improvement gates, then deterministically scores the feasible remainder. Selection remains a plan and creates no contact observation.
applicability: Checking deterministic support-expanding candidate selection at the certified configuration
Checking explicit collision, timing, mutation, detector-state, old-contact, and assistance refusals
failure_boundaries: Planner selection is not TOUCH, LOAD, BEARING, or proof of a physical catch
The certified candidate set, morphology, timing, target surface, and scaffold do not establish general transfer
No free 3D standing or bracing, generalized fall arrest, getting up, gait, walking, repair, or guidance is established
unknowns: How candidate generation and collision clearance should generalize across morphology and terrain
How model uncertainty should reduce the reachable deadline and support-improvement envelope

authoring.title: The certified contact coordinator requires observed TOUCH, LOAD, and BEARING
authoring.claim: In the exact certified BR10.1 fixtures, target arrival remains SEARCH until ground-qualified contact creates TOUCH; an available local normal-load witness creates LOAD; the full declared load and separation dwell creates BEARING; observed contact loss immediately revokes bearing; reacquisition returns through TOUCH; and duplicate ticks or nonfinite available loads fail closed.
authoring.scope: Only the exact contact-phase configuration, semantic ground qualification, local load availability, separating-speed witness, confirmation dwells, tick order, source, and BR10.1 program scope certified by br10_20260723T181129Z_980549f8.
authoring.mechanism: A strict state coordinator advances only from explicit observations. Target arrival has no transition authority, load cannot exist without an available witness, bearing requires sustained load and nonseparation, and loss revokes support immediately.
applicability: Separating planned target arrival from observed contact authority
Checking ordered contact acquisition, loss, and reacquisition at the certified thresholds
failure_boundaries: The local normal-load witness is not generalized per-foot allocation
Phase authority does not prove that a controller can reach or retain the contact
No free 3D standing or bracing, generalized fall arrest, getting up, gait, walking, repair, or guidance is established
unknowns: How compliant, intermittent, and multi-patch contacts should alter confirmation dwells
Which independently calibrated load witness should replace the local predicted-impulse instrument in a generalized limb

authoring.title: The certified two-link map transforms sagittal force commands through J-transpose
authoring.claim: In the exact certified BR10.2 fixtures, the strict finite sagittal map reports the analytic endpoint Jacobian, maps commanded tangent and unilateral normal force through J-transpose, agrees with finite-difference virtual work, mirrors only the tangent generalized component, preserves force-independent link gravity, exactly matches the accepted vertical-only map at zero tangent, carries command-not-measurement non-claims, and fails closed for missing, extra, unrecognized, nonfinite, nonnumeric, unilateral-invalid, or degenerate inputs.
authoring.scope: Only the exact two-link sagittal geometry, angles, masses, gravity, command fields, digest, strict-field boundary, source, and BR10.2 program scope certified by br10_20260723T181129Z_980549f8.
authoring.mechanism: The explicit two-link endpoint Jacobian maps a commanded tangent and normal contact-force pair into joint generalized forces using J-transpose, then adds link-gravity feedforward. It leaves the earlier vertical-only mapper unchanged.
applicability: Checking the analytic sagittal J-transpose mapping at the certified geometry
Checking zero-tangent parity and strict failure behavior without weakening the vertical-only contract
failure_boundaries: The mapped force pair is a command and not a measured contact load
The two-link sagittal map does not establish per-foot allocation or a free-3D wrench map
A correct map does not prove arbitrary limb strength, reachability, stability, fall arrest, gait, or walking
unknowns: How singularity handling and redundant allocation should work in more complex limbs
How compliance and actuator dynamics change commanded generalized force into observed contact response

authoring.title: The certified planar fixture creates a new bearing contact and returns to stance
authoring.claim: In the exact certified BR10.3 Godot/Jolt pair, the active fixture begins with one bearing left distal contact and one unloaded right catch limb, plans on the first post-disturbance observation, creates ordered new TOUCH, LOAD, and BEARING evidence within the declared clock and impact envelope, expands the measured support interval, and returns to the declared stance dwell through the complete horizon using bounded normal-load rate, friction-reserved sagittal commands, finite paired actuators, and complete receipts and contact capacity; the matched no-catch fixture reaches only a late high-speed crash contact and never returns.
authoring.scope: Only the exact inherited BR7 sagittal guide, preparation-only root freeze and release, rigid bodies, passive hinges, initial contact state, candidate target, impulse, timing, finite actuators, controller, thresholds, surface, timestep, solver, engine, source, and BR10.3 program scope certified by br10_20260723T181129Z_980549f8.
authoring.mechanism: After the preparation freeze is released with the declared impulse, the active world selects one support-expanding target, drives the unloaded limb through finite paired joint torques, accepts contact only from explicit observations, then uses friction-reserved tangent and bounded normal commands to retain the new ordinary contact and return the scaffolded body to stance. The no-catch world provides the matched crash control.
applicability: Checking one scaffold-constrained planar reachable new-contact catch against its matched no-catch crash control
Checking first-observation planning, observed contact phases, support expansion, finite actuation, receipts, and full-horizon retention
failure_boundaries: The material guide locks out-of-plane translation, roll, and yaw, and the preparation root freeze is part of the fixture
Commanded shares and the local predicted normal-load witness do not establish measured per-foot allocation
The exact morphology, target, surface, and small disturbance do not establish a general articulated load-bearing limb or generalized fall arrest
No free 3D standing or bracing, getting up, gait, walking, creature repair, or automatic guidance is established
unknowns: Whether the response remains stable after releasing out-of-plane degrees of freedom
How different morphologies, terrains, candidate sets, and disturbance magnitudes alter reachability and retention
How a generalized controller should transition from catch contact into free-3D balance or fall arrest
